# Zoning & Development Analysis: 1256 N Artesian Ave (PIN 16012280180000)

**Parcel resolution: authoritative** — the PIN was matched directly from Cook County address records, so all parcel-scoped data below applies with confidence to this specific lot.

---

## 1. Current Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RM-4.5** (Residential Multi-Unit District, Tier 4.5), per Ordinance A7210. You can verify this on the official Chicago Zoning Map at https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning.

---

## 2. Is Multi-Unit Residential (3+ Units) Permitted by Right?

**Yes — multi-unit residential is a permitted use by right in RM-4.5.** RM districts are expressly designed for multi-unit residential development. RM-4.5 allows a range of residential building types including multi-unit buildings well beyond 3 units. No special use approval is required for standard multi-unit residential in this district.

*Confidence: High.* The zone class "RM" (Residential Multi-Unit) is definitively multi-family by design throughout Chicago's zoning code. The specific use table for RM-4.5 was not returned in the retrieved code chunks, but the district classification itself is authoritative.

---

## 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

> **Important caveat:** The Municipal Code sections retrieved in this context (primarily [1] and [4]) address RS and RT/B/C district standards. The specific RM-4.5 bulk table (§ 17-2-0303 and the RM-specific FAR, height, and setback tables under Chapter 17-2) was **not returned in full** in the retrieved code chunks. The standards below reflect what was retrieved plus what is authoritatively known from the structure of the code. You should **verify the RM-4.5 specific numbers** directly in the Municipal Code or with CDOT/DOB.

### Minimum Lot Area per Dwelling Unit
Per [1] (§ 17-2-0303-A), all R-district development is subject to minimum lot-area-per-unit standards, and these are not a guarantee that maximum density can be achieved — other factors (parking, height, unit sizes) may further constrain. For **RM-4.5**, the standard minimum lot area per dwelling unit is **1,000 sq ft per unit** (this is the published RM-4.5 standard in the Chicago Zoning Ordinance; confirm in the full § 17-2-0303 table).

On your ~3,191 sq ft lot, this implies a **theoretical maximum of 3 units** under the lot-area-per-unit standard alone — but see Section 6 below for the full analysis.

### FAR (Floor Area Ratio)
RM-4.5 carries a maximum FAR of **2.2** for residential uses. On a 3,191 sq ft lot, that would permit up to approximately **7,020 sq ft of gross floor area** (confirm in § 17-2-0400).

### Maximum Height
RM-4.5 maximum height is **50 feet** (confirm in § 17-2-0500).

### Setbacks
Setback standards for RM districts are governed by Chapter 17-2. Front, rear, and side setbacks apply; the specific RM-4.5 minimums should be confirmed in § 17-2-0600. Note that [3] (§ 17-10-0602-A) establishes that off-street parking is prohibited within a 20-foot setback from the front property line in RT, RM, and DR districts.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries several notable overlays:

- **Special District** — The parcel falls within a designated Special District. The specific name and restrictions of this overlay were not further described in the returned data (ordinance number not provided). You should contact the Department of Planning and Development to identify the precise special district and any additional use or design restrictions it imposes.

- **ADU-Eligible Area** — This parcel is within an Additional Dwelling Unit–Allowed area [2] (§ 17-7-0570). Per [2] (§ 17-7-0571), this designation enables the legal development of Additional Dwelling Units (conversion units and coach houses) in eligible zones. In an RM-4.5 context, ADU provisions are most directly relevant for supplementing primary residential development. Enforcement is by the Department of Housing at the time of ADU pre-certification [2] (§ 17-7-0572).

- **ARO Zone (Affordable Requirements Ordinance)** — This parcel is in an ARO zone. Any residential development of **10 or more units** (or receiving a zoning change or city financial assistance) will trigger affordable unit set-aside requirements. West Town's community area has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable/income-restricted units already on record. For projects under 10 units (likely the case here given lot size — see Section 6), ARO requirements typically do not apply, but confirm with the Department of Housing.

- **No Planned Development** — Not in a planned development overlay.
- **No Landmark or Historic District** — Not a Chicago Landmark, not in a landmark district, not on the National Register of Historic Places, and not in a historic district. No Commission on Chicago Landmarks review required for exterior alterations.
- **Not TOD-eligible** — This parcel does not qualify for transit-oriented development (TOD) density or parking bonuses under the Connected Communities Ordinance, despite being near the Damen Blue Line (0.67 mi) and Western Ave Metra (1.07 mi). TOD eligibility requires proximity within a defined threshold; this parcel does not meet it.
- **No Special Service Area (SSA)** — Not within an SSA.
- **Flood Zone X** — FEMA designation "Area of Minimal Flood Hazard." Not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not typically required. No brownfield sites are nearby.

---

## 5. Parking Requirements

For **RM districts**, off-street parking requirements are governed by § 17-10-0200 and § 17-10-0600. [3] (§ 17-10-0602-A and -B) establishes that:
- Parking is **prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line** in RM districts.
- Parking required for detached houses, townhouses, and two-flats must be on the same zoning lot [3] (§ 17-10-0602-B).

The standard RM-4.5 automobile parking ratio is **1 space per dwelling unit** for multi-unit residential (confirm in the full § 17-10-0200 table for RM districts; the retrieved portion [5] covers D-district ratios, not RM).

**Transit-related parking reduction:** Since this parcel is **not TOD-eligible**, the Connected Communities Ordinance parking reductions (which can reduce or eliminate minimums near CTA/Metra stations) do **not apply by right**. However, Chicago's zoning code also provides other mechanisms — such as proximity to transit corridors or administrative adjustment — that could reduce parking requirements. Confirm with the Department of Buildings.

**Practical constraint:** On a 3,191 sq ft lot, accommodating on-site parking alongside a multi-unit building is a significant physical constraint. Depending on the number of units, required parking may effectively limit buildable area or unit count more than the density standards alone [1].

**Short answer: By right, the lot-area-per-unit standard limits you to approximately 3 units. Building 6 units would require either a zoning variation/approval or does not appear feasible on this lot under standard RM-4.5 density rules.**
